newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay shares leap as crisis ends, Reliance stars.
newsitem.headline: Bombay shares leap as crisis ends, Reliance stars.

text.p: Bombay shares rallied on Monday following the appointment of Inder Kumar Gujral as India's new prime minister and on growing confidence a pro-market 1997/98 (April-March) budget will be passed, dealers said.
Markets had endured three weeks of uncertainty and if the United Front alliance had not agreed on a successor to defeated Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda the country could have faced snap polls.
"After the long uncertainty, there is some good news in the market," said Vijay Pandya, chief dealer at Classic Share & Stock Brokers.
The benchmark 30-share index of the Bombay Stock Exchange rallied 101.54 points, or 2.75 percent, to a provisional close of 3,798.06.

The speaker of India's lower house, P.A. Sangma said the new prime minister wanted to push through parliament the budget proposed by former finance minister P.Chidambaram, whose party quit the government following Gujral's nomination.
A sizzling ten percent rally by Reliance Industries, India's top private firm ahead of the company's annual resuts due on Tuesday also buoyed overall market sentiment, traders said.
A Reuters poll of 28 securities firms showed Reliance would post a net profit of 12.06 billion rupees for 1996/97, recording a 7.63 percent fall over the same period a year ago.
Reliance is set to announce results on Tuesday for the financial year ended March 31, 1997.
"We are forecasting a net profit of 12.81 billion rupees," said Shoma Roy, an analyst at Daewoo Securities.

But traders said speculators were active in the stock, which attracted higher annualised carry forward charges of about 8.80 rupees per share on Saturday as it entered a no-delivery period on the Bombay bourse.
A no-delivery period allows speculators to buy the stock without taking delivery for about a month.
Overall the market was reassured by the choice of Gujral to lead the country, and there was speculation he would persuade Chidambaram to return to the finance ministry.
The former finance minister's Tamil Maanila Congress quit the government in protest that its own leader G.K. Moopanar had been overlooked.
Gujral told reporters after taking the oath of office on Monday that he had decided to keep the foreign and finance ministry portfolios for himself.
"In Mr Gujral, the market is quite hopeful," said Neeraj Roy, head of institutional sales at Prime Broking.
"As things stand today, the budget is expected to be passed without any significant changes."
The 77-year-old new prime minister is due to face a vote of confidence in the lower house of parliament on Tuesday at 11 a.m. (0530 GMT).
Parliament is due to take up the budget proposals for 1997/98 (April-March) after it reassembles on April 30.
Foreign funds on Monday were buyers in blue chips including MTNL, Mahindra & Mahindra, HPCL and Colgate, traders said.
